MWE:

set_option doc.verso true

/-- Works: {kw (of := «term_<_»)}`<` -/
def lt_ok := 1

/-- Fails: {kw (of := «term_≤_»)}`≤` -/
def le_fails := 1

/-- Fails: {kw (of := «term_∧_»)}`∧` -/
def and_fails := 1

I noticed this while bumping a library, where the keyword role show errors on some notations.

I don't really understand this, and claude said this is a bug in core so I'm posting here, apologies in advance if this isn't the right place.

Claude's analysis

The {kw (of := ...)} docstring role fails for notations that core now declares with unicode(...), e.g. ≤, ≥, ∧, ∨ (Init/Notation.lean:375-405, changed in lean4#10384). {kw (of := «term_<_»)}<` still works since < is a plain infix:50 " < "`.

The atom checker in Lean/Elab/DocString/Builtin/Keywords.lean (containsAtom and its three siblings) matches ParserDescr.symbol and ParserDescr.nonReservedSymbol but has no arm for ParserDescr.unicodeSymbol, so the walk falls through and reports no atom. The same arms are still absent on current master, so this is not fixed by the recent docstring parser rewrite (lean4#15064). A bare {kw}≤` instead finds unrelated syntaxes that spell ≤ with a plain symbol (grind_filterGen≤_, binderPred≤_), which confirms term_≤_` is invisible to it.

apparently {kw} just fails inside any module file for all notation. Noticed this while moving a project to the module system.

module
set_option doc.verso true
/-- {kw (of := «term_<_»)}`<` -/
def a := 1
/-- {kw}`<` -/
def b := 1

claude diagnosis

Delete the module line and the same file compiles. {name} and {lean} roles are fine in module files.

Likely cause: kindHasAtoms in Lean/Elab/DocString/Builtin/Keywords.lean does if let some d := ci.value? then exprContainsAtoms d atoms, and in a module the body of an imported, non-exposed ParserDescr constant such as «term_<_» is not available, so the walk never sees the atoms. That is the same code path as the unicodeSymbol gap above. Neither core nor Mathlib uses {kw} in a module file, which would explain how it went unnoticed.

{kw! (of := «term_<_»)} works in both settings (it skips the atom check and only verifies the kind exists), so that is what I'm using as the workaround, with the caveat that it renders as plain code rather than a linked keyword.
This topic was moved here from #lean4 > {kw} docstring role fails for unicode(...) notations like ≤ by Michael Rothgang.
